m1-build-unit-tests.title: Build src/physics/layer2/fp_gate_real_extractor.py + unit tests
m1-build-unit-tests.imperative: Implement make_extractor(*, year, weekends, db_path, sessions=('FP2','FP3'), max_drivers=None, max_laps_per_driver=None, cache=None) -> GateExtractor in a NEW file src/physics/layer2/fp_gate_real_extractor.py, satisfying the GateExtractor Protocol (fp_observations/q_targets) exactly against the frozen RawFpObservation/RawQTarget shapes in fp_gate.py -- do NOT edit fp_gate.py/fp_representativeness.py/GATE_PROTOCOL. Reuse session_fit.load_quali_session, session_braking._driver_samples (one shared cache dict per (weekend,session) namespace to avoid cross-session collisions -- _driver_samples' cache key is (driver, refine) with no session component, so a literal single flat dict shared across FP2/FP3/Q would silently return the wrong session's samples; namespace by session to stay safe while still reusing one instance-owned container), apex_extract.extract_apex_observations, capability.apex_pace, fp_lap_latent.extract_fp_lap_latent, mass_model.fp_mass, session_race.session_cumulative_track_laps. Map driver->constructor via session_classifications (read-only sqlite, mirroring session_race.py's _ro_uri/_get_session_id pattern). Emit ONE RawFpObservation per (constructor, session): hours_to_q from a nominal clock schedule (FP1=26,FP2=22,FP3=3,Q=0), grip_value=ApexPace.pace pooled per constructor, power_value=None, latent=the constructor's fastest-clean-lap FpLapLatent, track_evolution via session_cumulative_track_laps, session_max_track_evolution=None, fp_mass_sigma_kg=mass_model.fp_mass(year).sigma_kg. Never raise on a missing driver/session -- log and skip. physics-region only: no evo/latent_power/compound_prior/fastf1 imports. Write tests/unit/physics/layer2/test_fp_gate_real_extractor.py: unit-test the pure helpers (nominal clock schedule lookup, per-car grip assembly via capability.apex_pace on synthetic ApexObservation lists, lap-time-based lap capping) on synthetic inputs, plus a mock-session test of fp_observations/q_targets shape correctness -- do NOT load real telemetry in this test file. Test mode is test-after (compute-glue over reviewed seams): TDD red/green split does not apply; go straight to green. Attest any check:null precondition before start. Attach the diff or new-file listing as evidence when advancing.

postconditions.statement: fp_gate_real_extractor.py implements make_extractor/GateExtractor against the frozen Protocol; unit tests (pure helpers + mock-session) pass

constraints: never raise on missing driver/session -- skip with logged reason

m2-real-smoke.title: Real integration smoke: Hungary 2023 FP2, 4 drivers, 2 laps/driver
m2-real-smoke.imperative: Foreground-run: instantiate make_extractor(year=2023, weekends=['Hungary'], db_path='data/f1_data_2023.db', sessions=('FP2',), max_drivers=4, max_laps_per_driver=2) and call fp_observations('Hungary'). Capture the observation count and one RawFpObservation repr. This reads real telemetry and may take several minutes -- run it with a bounded timeout; if it does not finish, capture partial output/logs and note it honestly, that is an acceptable outcome per the handoff. Confirm `git status --short data/` is clean (read-only run, no DB writes). Attach the captured output as evidence, then attest.

postconditions.statement: real smoke output (observation count + one repr, or honest partial+note) captured and attached; git status --short data/ clean

why_trail.why: Handoff is complete (task/intent/scope/exclusions/evidence/test-mode/stop-conditions all present); fp_gate.py:65-176 confirms RawFpObservation/RawQTarget frozen shapes and GateExtractor Protocol (fp_observations/q_targets). Seams confirmed by reading source: session_fit.load_quali_session(year,gp,session_type,cache=DEFAULT_CACHE) returns (session,rho,fallback); session_braking._driver_samples(session,driver,cache=dict) returns (processed_df,control_df,raw_xyz,raw_speed) with processed_df carrying a lap_number column across concatenated flying laps; apex_extract.extract_apex_observations accepts a per-lap DataFrame; capability.apex_pace pools {car_id:[ApexObservation]}->ApexPace(pace,...); fp_lap_latent.extract_fp_lap_latent(year,gp,session_type,db_path=) returns per-lap FpLapLatent list; mass_model.fp_mass(year).sigma_kg; session_race.session_cumulative_track_laps(year,gp,session_type,constructor,db_path) matches handoff exactly. session_classifications schema confirmed (year,round_num,gp_name,session_type,driver_id,driver_name,team,position,points,status). Noted a real risk: _driver_samples caches on (driver,refine) with no session component, so a single flat shared dict across FP2/FP3/Q would leak the wrong session's samples -- will namespace per (weekend,session_type).

Implemented src/physics/layer2/fp_gate_real_extractor.py: RealGateExtractor + make_extractor factory satisfying GateExtractor (fp_observations/q_targets), constructing frozen RawFpObservation/RawQTarget from fp_gate.py unmodified. Pure helpers (nominal_hours_to_q, cap_laps_by_time, lap_frames, per_car_grip_values) unit-tested on synthetic inputs; a mock-session test monkeypatches load_quali_session/_driver_samples/extract_apex_observations against a tiny synthetic sqlite fixture DB (no real telemetry) and asserts fp_observations/q_targets shape (2 constructors, correct session_type/hours_to_q/None power/latent type/fp_mass_sigma_kg). Key deviation from a literal reading of the handoff: the shared _driver_samples cache is namespaced per (weekend_id,session_type) rather than one flat dict, because _driver_samples' own cache key (driver,refine) has no session component -- a flat shared dict across FP2/FP3/Q would silently leak one session's samples into another; a regression test (test_shared_cache_is_namespaced_per_session) asserts this. pytest: 13/13 passed.
